quick_skim.title: Reason What Matters: Retrieval-Grounded Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
quick_skim.abstract: Universal multimodal embedding (UME) learns unified representations across modalities, enabling a single model to support diverse retrieval tasks. Recent methods use Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning to better interpret multimodal inputs before generating embeddings for complex retrieval tasks and further optimize this reasoning process through GRPO with retrieval-based rewards. However, two limitations hinder corpus-scale deployment. GRPO assigns all CoT tokens the same advantage, without identifying input-supported claims or evidence that distinguishes the positive from negatives. Moreover, generating a complete CoT before each embedding introduces substantial latency, even when a partial trace already provides sufficient retrieval evidence. To address these limitations, we propose Reason What Matters (ReWAM), a retrieval-grounded reasoning framework that uses retrieval feedback to guide both credit assignment and reasoning computation. Specifically, we introduce Retrieval-aware Self-Distillation (RASD), which constructs privileged guidance from input-supported evidence that distinguishes the positive item from retrieved hard negatives. An on-policy self-teacher uses this guidance to refine trajectory-level feedback into token-specific supervision for retrieval-relevant reasoning. We further develop Retrieval-adaptive Inference (RAI), which uses a retrieval confidence head to estimate the remaining retrieval utility of a partial CoT. It stops unproductive traces early and accelerates useful continuations with speculative decoding. Extensive experiments on MMEB-V2 and MRMR demonstrate that ReWAM achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance while delivering up to 5x the inference throughput of competitive explicit-CoT UME methods. These results bridge the gap between retrieval quality and inference efficiency, making reasoning-enhanced UME practical for large-scale deployment.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Universal multimodal embedding uses CoT reasoning but wastes tokens and latency. This work grounds reasoning in retrieval evidence to select what matters, improving embedding quality and efficiency.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 通用多模态嵌入通过统一表示支持多种跨模态检索任务，但现有方法依赖完整思维链推理，既未区分有效证据又带来显著延迟。本文提出以检索为接地的推理机制，识别输入支撑的关键证据并裁剪冗余推理轨迹，从而在生成嵌入前聚焦真正有用的信息。实验表明该方法在提升跨模态对齐与检索质量的同时降低了推理开销，有助于语料级部署。

quick_skim.title: ViCo-SAM3: Vision-Conditioned Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Camouflaged Object Segmentation
quick_skim.abstract: Open-vocabulary camouflaged object segmentation (OVCOS) aims to segment unseen camouflaged objects under text guidance. We observe that SAM3 still suffers from a pronounced semantic gap between global textual semantics and fine-grained pixel-level visual cues in OVCOS. Meanwhile, fully fine-tuning the text encoder introduces heavy parameter overhead and risks overfitting to training categories, which compromises open-vocabulary representation flexibility. To address these issues, we propose ViCo-SAM3, a Vision-Conditioned alignment framework designed for OVCOS. Specifically, we introduce vision-conditioned (ViCo) module, which dynamically modulates text embeddings with global visual context, enabling textual representations to adapt to the current image content and thereby effectively bridging the semantic gap between vision and text. Building on this, we further design a vision-conditioned cross-modal binding (ViCoBind) module to enhance cross-modal interaction and semantic alignment between visual and textual representations. Without bells and whistles, ViCo-SAM3 achieves state-of-the-art performance on the OVCamo benchmark and demonstrates strong generalization.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: OVCOS suffers a semantic gap between global text semantics and pixel-level visual cues; ViCo-SAM3 uses a vision-conditioned module to modulate text embeddings with global visual context, improving alignment without full text-encoder fine-tuning.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 开放词汇伪装目标分割要求模型在文本引导下分割未见过的伪装目标，但SAM3存在全局文本语义与像素级视觉线索之间的语义鸿沟，完全微调文本编码器又带来参数开销与过拟合风险。本文提出ViCo-SAM3，通过视觉条件模块用全局视觉上下文动态调制文本嵌入，使文本表示适应细粒度视觉线索。该方法在保持开放词汇表示灵活性的同时缩小了跨模态语义差距。其视觉条件对齐思路可迁移到其他文本-视觉跨模态对齐任务。
